docs.article:
Make it look good#

You uploaded a GLB and nothing looks good: it is dark, flat, the first view faces a window, and the Lights, Sun and Exterior panels are a lot of sliders. One button does the whole job — the best picture this engine can make of your scene, and the best walkthrough — and you can undo it.

Where the button is#

  • In the toolbar beside Lights and Sun: Make it look good (the sparkle). One click.
  • On the Ready card that appears when a scene opens, when the scene is live-lit and has no lights of its own — the upload this was built for.
  • On a link: add &auto=1 and it runs when the scene opens. &auto=0 switches it off for that link (nothing is touched, even if the link carries a saved look).
  • In the embed SDK: viewer.autoLook() (see embed-sdk.md).

While it works the chip reads Looking… view 3/8, Looking… sun 7/12, Looking… exposure. It takes about ten seconds on a laptop: every step measures the real frame and moves on only when the picture confirms it.

What it does, in order#

  1. Picks the first view. It stands at each of the auto tour's waypoints and at the room's centre facing four ways, and scores each view by composition: how much of the frame is the room (surfaces between arm's length and the far wall), variety in depth, in surface orientation and in materials (a sofa, a table and a plant beat a blank wall or a window decal), no near-plane clipping, and — indoors — a penalty for every ray that leaves through a window into nothing. The horizon is put on the upper third. The best view is where you start.
  2. Measures the frame. The rendered frame becomes a luminance histogram: median, 5th and 95th percentiles.
  3. Fixes exposure. Up to four steps toward a median of 0.40 with the 95th percentile under 0.95 (no clipped whites), inside the Lights panel's ±4 EV. This alone rescues most "nothing can be seen" uploads.
  4. Checks baked or live. Environment fill off for one frame: a lightmap-baked scene barely changes, a live-lit one goes dark. A baked scene gets the quality knobs and keeps its own exposure — EV 0 unless its highlights clip (then down, at most one stop) or it is far too dark (then up); never a sun, never a fill (the bake is the light).
  5. Places the sun. Indoors it tries 12 azimuths with only the sun on and keeps the one that puts the most direct light on what you see (through the openings); outdoors it stands 35° off the model's long axis on the camera's side. 32° up. If your file has its own lights or emissive materials they are kept and scaled as a group so the median lands.
  6. Fill and shadows. Soft sun shadows (Lights panel's Shadow softness 3), then the environment fill is raised until the deepest shadows clear (5th percentile ≥ 0.04) while the 95th stays under 0.95 — shadows lifted, contrast kept — and exposure is re-balanced.
  7. Sky for exteriors. A scene that reads as an exterior (the compiler says open, or a large open footprint whose depth probe mostly misses within 30 m) gets the physical sky at turbidity 2.5, fog off. Interiors never get a sky.
  8. Every quality knob the device has. Ambient occlusion and the mirror probe and screen-space reflections (WebGPU only), glass refraction, and Cinematic path tracing on WebGPU — the walkthrough plays in raster, and whenever the camera rests the picture converges to the path-traced frame. Full render scale is pinned on re-open (scale=1).
  9. Starts the walkthrough. Your guided tour if you authored one; else the auto tour, joined at the chosen view rather than from its start. Under prefers-reduced-motion the camera stands at the view instead of flying. The chip reads Playing the walkthrough · Stop.
  10. Keeps it. The link now carries everything the panels would have written (?lights=, ?sun=, ?sky=, ?ssao=, ?ssr=, ?glass=, ?cinematic=, ?scale=, the view as ?at=) plus auto=1, so anyone opening it gets the lit scene and the walkthrough without pressing anything. If you are the scene's signed-in owner, the look is also saved into the scene's default experience, so the plain link opens lit for every visitor.

The two looks#

The routine now picks one of two looks and the Lights panel's Look row lets you switch with one tap (no camera move, no walkthrough):

  • Showroom — the first look for a live-lit interior without authored lights (the reception uploaded from Blender). Even, soft, high-key: a strong neutral studio fill, a gentle key sun for shape, Khronos PBR Neutral tone mapping (the glTF reference curve — off-white walls land near white instead of ACES's grey), subtle AO, and a light backdrop behind the windows and around the outside view. Exposure is metered on the walls: the frame's 90th-percentile luma lands near sRGB 232 without the 99th clipping. No sun sweep, no Cinematic (real GI would darken it). A room with nothing light to meter on (every surface near black even at +2.5 EV) takes daylight instead.
  • Realistic daylight — the sun + sky look the routine always made: the sun sampled over 12 azimuths, environment fill lifted until the shadows read, the physical sky for exteriors, Cinematic when it agrees.

Baked scenes get neither (only exposure, as before); scenes with their own lights stay as exported; exteriors take daylight. &look=showroom / &look=daylight on a link pins the choice; the button writes it beside lights= so a shared link opens the same way. Products in Fidelity keep the studio look they already had.

A first open also frames the outside view like a product viewer: a 35° lens with the model filling about three quarters of the frame, resting at a 3/4 angle on the façade side instead of turning on the turntable. Walking keeps the 55° a room needs. &framing=0 restores the old framing; &fov= / &fill= tune it.

What it never touches#

  • Your model, its materials and its textures (nothing recompiles).
  • Lightmaps: a baked scene keeps its bake; only exposure and the quality knobs move.
  • Your authored hotspots, cards and guided tour (it plays them).
  • Weather, fog and the ground you set in the Exterior panel (it only turns the sky on for exteriors; it turns nothing off).
  • Anything a visitor cannot see: it never writes to the server unless you are the signed-in owner, and then only the default experience.

Undo#

  • Right after a run a small popover under the toolbar shows what was chosen (sun, fill, exposure, medians) with Undo: lights, sun, sky, Cinematic, the quality knobs, the camera and the link go back to the state before the click.
  • Later: Lights → Reset returns every light setting to the file's; the Sun and Exterior panels have their own controls; and &auto=0 on a link keeps the routine from running at all.

What the numbers mean (for QA)#

window.__verseAutoLook.result holds the whole decision: before / after (median, p5, p95), view and composition (score, coverage, depth spread, orientation and material variety, misses, candidates), sun and the 12 sunSamples, look (showroom / daylight), backdrop, ev / env / all / soft, sky, quality (ssao, probe, ssr, glass, cinematic, scale), walkthrough, lights (the share string) and persisted; steps is the log. Gates: web/test/fix-verify-autolook.mjs and, for the showroom look, web/test/fix-verify-showroom.mjs (the reception against reference captures: wall luminance, corner floor, glass, sharpness, idle DRS).

Unbaked interiors: lighting that bounces#

Scenes uploaded without a bake (live materials, "Lighting = Keep as exported") now get real-time global illumination: light from the windows, the sun, lamps and glowing materials bounces around the room, corners darken, colours bleed, a closed room stays dark. There is nothing to switch on — it is computed when the scene is compiled and runs in the viewer on every device. It follows the Sun panel, the sun study and the light studio within a fraction of a second, and Make it look good waits for it before it sets the exposure (rooms usually come out a little darker and more natural than before, so the button raises the exposure to match). Baked scenes are not changed. To compare, add ?gi=0 to the link. Re-upload a scene compiled before 4.0 to get it.

Honest limits#

  • The measurements are of the frame on screen, so the viewport's size and the device shape the result a little; a link re-opened on another device replays the saved knobs rather than re-measuring.
  • Texture detail is already streamed at the device's maximum by proximity (there is no cap to lift), and foliage effects are compile-time lanes (always on when the file has them) — the button reports both as-is.
  • Baked-or-live: for a streamed scene the renderer knows (over half of its surfaces lightmap-baked, checked before exposure moves); otherwise it is a measurement (fill off → does the frame change?), not a flag; a scene that is half baked, half live is treated as live.
  • The composition score is a heuristic over nine depth probes per view; on a scene with no auto tour only the centre views are tried.
